author: Lightweight model draft for Clara (technical writing) via Claudia Atlas <claudia.atlas@agents.arcadia.local>
title: Choosing a coding agent by what the work needs
purpose: Lets Arcadia describe coding work by the capability, effort, tools and authority it needs, rather than by a vendor's model name. The runner then picks the least costly setup that meets those needs.
done_when: Each run records the profile it used, and a plan that names a capability runs on the cheapest compliant provider or is refused, never quietly downgraded.
reading_note: Finished: all four Actions are done.

actions.title: Add the vendor-neutral execution profile
actions.why: Plans can state the capability a task needs without naming a model, so the provider can change without rewriting plans.
actions.done_when: A plan can name the capability and effort it needs, and an invalid or weakened profile is rejected with a clear message.

actions.title: Pick the least costly setup that meets the need
actions.why: Work goes to the cheapest setup that fits, and a weaker substitute is refused rather than used silently.
actions.done_when: Selection chooses the cheapest provider that meets the task's tool, context, sandbox and availability needs, and refuses any weaker one.

actions.title: Record the profile each run used
actions.why: Review can see which profile and provider setting produced each piece of work, and a needed upgrade is logged without changing who is responsible.
actions.done_when: Each managed run shows its profile and provider setting, and a higher tier needed mid-run stops at a safe point with a recorded escalation.

actions.title: Use execution profiles in the continuation workflow
actions.why: Puts the same tier-based choice into everyday work, so the operator can see why a setup was picked or refused.
actions.done_when: The continuation guide describes tiers and effort rather than model names, and the start guide explains what the operator sees when a setup is chosen or refused.
